name: Isolated Acheiria

criteria.description: Complete congenital absence of one hand without involvement of other limbs
No associated skeletal or systemic malformations detected
Normal chromosomal and genetic testing excluding syndromic causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence of one hand with no other limb or systemic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and exclusion of syndromic conditions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of distal forearm structures on affected side
searchTerms: missing lower arm bones on one side
no wrist or forearm bones on affected side

common.symptomName: Residual limb hypoplasia proximal to absent hand
searchTerms: small residual limb proximal to absent hand
hypoplastic limb segment near missing hand

common.symptomName: Compensatory overuse of contralateral upper limb
Mild functional limitation in fine motor tasks

occasional.symptomName: Phantom limb sensations in absent hand region
Mild ipsilateral shoulder girdle muscle atrophy
searchTerms: mild muscle wasting in shoulder area
shoulder muscle thinning on same side

occasional.symptomName: Psychological distress related to limb absence
searchTerms: mental stress due to limb absence

occasional.symptomName: Mild scoliosis secondary to asymmetrical posture
searchTerms: mild spine curvature from uneven posture

rare.symptomName: Associated ipsilateral upper arm bone hypoplasia
searchTerms: underdeveloped upper arm bone on same side

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous scarring or skin tags at amputation site
searchTerms: scars or skin tags at amputation site
skin marks where limb was removed

rare.symptomName: Mild vascular anomalies in affected limb
searchTerms: minor blood vessel abnormalities in limb
mild vascular changes in affected arm
small blood vessel issues near limb

imaging: X-ray showing absence of hand bones with normal proximal limb structures
MRI to exclude associated soft tissue anomalies
genetic: No pathogenic variants detected in limb development genes in isolated cases
other: Clinical examination confirming isolated unilateral hand absence without syndromic features

redFlags: Presence of multiple limb anomalies suggesting syndromic etiology
references: Kumar S, et al. Congenital absence of hand: clinical and radiological features. J Pediatr Orthop. 2018.
Genetics Home Reference: Limb reduction defects
